newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds looking shaky, may slip to 113-13.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds looking shaky, may slip to 113-13.

text.p: September T-bond futures have broken an intraday uptrend, paving the way for losses to 113-13, technical analysts said on Monday.
But a bounce off an initial retracement level of 114-17 could put the market back on an upward track.

Raynard Cheng, analyst at First Chicago in London, favoured a scenario whereby T-bonds slide through 114-00 and find support at 113-13, a 38 percent retracement of the rally from 110-23 on June 30 to the July 17 peak of 115-02.
By 0945 GMT, September T-bonds were 6/32 down at 114-00.

Cheng said the price action since 115-02 was disappointing. And even if September resurfaced above 114-17, the base of the Thursday's spike, second and third retracement levels could still hamper gains.
"But if it can recover above 114-17 then it can stabilise and eventually go to 115-02, and then 116-17. That means the resumption of the uptrend," Cheng said.
On the downside and below 113-13, Cheng saw support coming in more crucially at 112-28 which is a 50 percent retracement of the June 30 to July 17 rally.
"We're looking for that as an intraday target," Cheng said.

Technical analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said in a research note the inability to put much distance from the 114-01 low by the close on Friday and a likely five wave pattern lower suggested that after a bounce to 114-11, T-bonds could slip toward 113-23/21.
The first of those levels was a wave projection off 114-11 while 113-21 was the 76.4 percent retracement back to the 113-07 low on July 15 from the 115-02 high.
"The key for going forward is that bonds not trade below 113-07," DMG analysts said, adding that a move below there would put September in danger of at least another point or two of correction.
"Our expectation though is that the five wave move off 113-07 was the start of a larger five wave pattern that will ultimately take futures up to 117/118 by mid-August," they added.
At the short end, December Eurodollar futures were 0.015 down on the day at 94.040.
